claims.text: High configurational entropy in refractory HEAs causes sluggish diffusion of both metal and oxygen species.
Sluggish diffusion enables controlled, self-healing segregation of Cr and Al at the metal/oxide interface.
Interfacial segregation of reactive elements promotes formation and long-term retention of a continuous, adherent protective oxide scale.
The protective scale may consist of Cr2O3, Al2O3, or a related spinel.
The proposed initial material is a homogeneous, single-phase AlCoCrFeNiTi-type HEA with a near-random elemental distribution.
The proposed intervention is static oxidation in air at approximately 800–900 °C for an extended duration.
High configurational entropy controls elemental partitioning at the oxide-scale/metal interface through its effect on diffusion.
Reduced diffusion limits depletion of Cr and Al from the alloy near the interface.
Reduced diffusion promotes controlled enrichment of Cr and Al at the oxide/metal interface.
Limited but sustained outward cation diffusion and oxygen ingress provide self-healing of the oxide scale.
Relative to a lower-entropy conventional alloy, the HEA will form a thinner and more uniform oxide scale.
Relative to the baseline, the HEA oxide scale will be more adherent and resistant to spallation.
Oxidation of the HEA will exhibit parabolic kinetics.
A lower-configurational-entropy alloy with comparable reactive-element concentration typically has faster diffusion.
Faster diffusion in the baseline causes thicker, less adherent, and more spallation-prone oxide scales.
The proposed mechanism applies in air at approximately 800–900 °C when the HEA contains sufficient concentrations of protective-oxide-forming elements such as Cr or Al.
Reactive-element concentration can affect the high-temperature oxidation behavior of an HEA.
The mechanism may cease to apply outside the protective-oxide-forming composition regime or when oxide volatilization dominates.
The controlled comparison holds oxidation temperature, atmosphere, duration, and reactive-element concentration approximately constant while varying configurational entropy.
The hypothesis is falsified if the HEA shows no statistically significant improvement, or performs worse, in scale continuity, oxidation kinetics, or adhesion relative to the lower-entropy control.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is framed specifically around refractory HEAs, but the principal example and proposed test alloy are AlCoCrFeNiTi-type materials, which are not clearly established here as refractory HEAs.
